lines.text: WEL COME TO ROYAL MANAS NATIONAL PARK

notes: Painted wooden entrance board of Royal Manas National Park, mid-distance. Paint is weathered: in the first line 'O ROYAL' and 'NA' of NATIONAL are mostly faded and the final K of PARK is lost at the edge. Four small Dzongkha lines above the English are too small and faded at 1600 px to transcribe and are NOT included. WWF logo bottom right; a person and a van in the background.

author: Christopher J. Fynn
attribution: Photo: Christopher J. Fynn, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Womanang_primary_school_sign_(Trashiyangtse).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: Womnang mide lobdra chungwa (Womanang community primary school)

notes: Hand-painted red school board. Dzongkha line 1 starts with a head mark (yig mgo, transcribed as ༄); its first letter is read as a-chung (འོམ, pronounced 'wom'); the last letter before the shad is read as བ. Line 2 uses the contracted spelling བཀྲིས (for བཀྲ་ཤིས). Date separators are tildes.

lines.latin: Pelden Druk Zhung (Royal Government of Bhutan)
Sonam dang Nagtshel Lhenkhag (Ministry of Agriculture and Forests)

notes: Red printed board, frontal and sharp, Paro. Logos left (seedling) and right (blue cross). In the last Dzongkha line there is a space (no visible tsek) between ཟམ་པ and སྤ་རོ.

author: Leovdvxxx
attribution: Photo: Leovdvxxx, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sarpang_post_office_2008_685kb.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Name board at the top of Sarpang post office (1280 px photo, board small in frame). A short Dzongkha line at the board's top right and a cut-off 'POST' logo top left are too small to transcribe. Distractors: 'POST OFFICE / Education for every girl and boy' poster at left, red post box at right. Two staff and children stand in the doorway (incidental, not the subject).

author: Dr Vikramjit Kakati
attribution: Photo: Dr Vikramjit Kakati, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Trashiyangtse.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Welcome message painted on a green boulder at the entrance of Trashiyangtse town; 'T/YANGTSE' abbreviates Trashi Yangtse, and its G is painted without a bar (looks like C). 'WELCOMETO' is painted with almost no space. The first Dzongkha syllable is crudely painted (read as བྱོན, the standard welcome phrase); the other syllables are clear. Distractors: 'DZONG' arrow board, blue police surveillance notice, 'LET'S KEEP YANGTSE CLEAN' stones.

author: Bernard Gagnon
attribution: Photo: Bernard Gagnon, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gyelwang_Lam,_Thimphu,_Bhutan.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Red/yellow arrow street sign in Thimphu. Dzongkha uses Tibetan digits ༢-༡༢. Faded remains of older lettering (a Dzongkha cluster at left, 'LAM' at right) show through the paint. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

lines.latin: Druk Sherab Thrulrig Ling (Bhutan education and technology park)

lines.text: THE BHUTAN EDUCATION AND TECHNOLOGY ACADEMY PARK PRIVATE LIMITED
PO Box No. 1711, Chamjeykha, Kabisa, Kawang, Thimphu - 11001

expect.query: Bhutan Education and Technology Academy Park

notes: Red entrance board of BETA Park, Kabisa (Thimphu). Dzongkha line starts with a head mark (transcribed ༄). 'nd' of 2nd is superscript. Separators in the contact line are double backslashes. A partly hidden 'NO TRESPASSING ... SITE VISIT' board at right is a distractor. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

lines.latin: Khamsum Yulley (victorious over the three realms)
Namgyal Choeten kyi chinlam (path to Namgyal Chorten)

notes: Painted direction panel set in a wall (Punakha valley), arrow pointing left. Line 1 starts with a head mark (transcribed ༄). The second-to-last syllable of Dzongkha line 2 is read as ཕྱིན (ph vs b not fully certain in the brush lettering); the rest is clear. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

lines.latin: Druk Gyelyong Pemdzö dang Yigrig Tenjog Khang (National Library and Archives of Bhutan)
Nangsi dang Söldzin Lhenkhag (Ministry of Home and Cultural Affairs)

notes: Large maroon name board, frontal, Thimphu. Only the name block is labelled; the Dzongkha visiting-hours line and the small English visiting hours / phone / email / bookshop lines below are not transcribed. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Afifa Afrin
attribution: Photo: Afifa Afrin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Highway_direction_board_in_Bhutan.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Three green highway direction panels on a gantry near Phuentsholing, shot from below. The Dzongkha line on the Tsimasham panel (four syllables) is not transcribed: its letters are too uncertain at this size. The T of TSIMASHAM carries a small dot/accent below it.

author: Gerd Eichmann
attribution: Photo: Gerd Eichmann, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Trongsa-Bjee_Zam-Bruecke-06-Schild-2015-gje.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Steel bridge plaque (Trongsa district); the target is the right-hand data panel. The left panel (Bhutan and Japan flags, 'THE JAPANESE OFFICIAL DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE PROJECT ...', small Dzongkha and Japanese dedication, 2004. 3) is a distractor and not transcribed.

author: Wiki.cullin
attribution: Photo: Wiki.cullin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Road_to_Paro_Airport_-_Bhutan.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Three green overhead direction panels at a junction near Paro, small in frame (mid-distance). Panels read left to right; distances 06 and 22 km with turn arrows. Drukgyel Dzong is spelled 'DRUGYEL' on the sign.

attribution: Photo: Bernard Gagnon, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Royal_Takin_Preserve,_Bhutan_01.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: Gyeldzin dronggyimtse gyünkyong sakhong (Royal takin preserve)

lines.text: DEPARTMENT OF FOREST AND PARK SERVICES

notes: Red entrance board set in a tiled wall, Motithang (Thimphu); emblems left and right. Dzongkha line 1 starts with a head mark (transcribed ༄). In the takin word the syllable read as ཙེ could be ཚེ (the aspirated form); checker should confirm. Emblem micro-text not transcribed. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Erik Charlton
attribution: Photo: Erik Charlton, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/78042080@N00/49117911133. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Blue lit shop board over the door of a painted building in Paro town, wide-angle dusk shot. Dzongkha line starts with a head mark (transcribed ༄). The round 'SONAM TROPHEL RESTAURANT' hanging sign at right is a distractor; shoppers in the doorway and passers-by at right are incidental.

lines.latin: Sönam Tashi natshog tshongkhang (Sonam Tashi general store)

notes: Blue cloth banner over a shop in Paro bazaar, slightly wrinkled. 'བཀྲ་ཤི' is written without the final ས on the sign. The two small lines below ('...als in all kinds of: UTAINSIL, STATIONERIES, SPORTS GOODS, GIFT ITEMS, / ...SMETICS ITEMS, GROCERY ITEMS &etc. Ph.No:271356.') are cut at the left edge and not part of the label.
